item.title: 6 Best AI Risk Management Certifications, Training Programs, and Courses
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: November 3, 2025
Tags: ["AI Risk Management", "Certifications and Training", "AI Governance", "Compliance and Ethics", "Security"]
Summary:
  • AI risk management certifications are vital for responsible AI adoption.
  • Global standards like NIST and EU AI Act guide these programs.
  • Certifications teach skills in compliance, ethics, and security.
  • Programs range from beginner to expert levels.
  • They prepare professionals for roles in AI governance and risk mitigation.

item.title: AI Risk Management Framework: 4 Core Functions Explained
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: November 3, 2025
Tags: ["AI Risk Management", "AI Governance", "Regulatory Compliance", "NIST Framework", "Ethical AI"]
Summary:
  • The NIST AI Risk Management Framework helps manage AI risks across the lifecycle.
  • It is voluntary but widely adopted globally.
  • The framework has four core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage.
  • It aligns with regulations like the EU AI Act and ISO/IEC standards.
  • The framework supports ethical, accountable, and compliant AI system development.
  • Organizations use it to build trustworthy AI governance programs.

item.title: What is AI Risk Management? Strategies, Best Practices & More
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: November 3, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Risk Management", "Cybersecurity", "Compliance", "Ethics"]
Summary:
  • AI risk management identifies and mitigates AI-specific threats.
  • It uses frameworks like NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC standards.
  • Risks include bias, model drift, and adversarial attacks.
  • Continuous monitoring ensures AI systems stay safe and ethical.
  • Compliance with regulations like the EU AI Act is crucial.
  • Effective AI risk management builds trust and business resilience.

item.title: Bypassing Azure AI Content Safety Guardrails
item.description:
Author: William Hackett
Date: January 14, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Cloud Computing", "Microsoft Azure", "Content Moderation", "Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities"]
Summary:
  • Mindgard found two security flaws in Azure AI Content Safety guardrails.
  • These flaws let attackers bypass AI Text Moderation and Prompt Shield.
  • Bypassing allows harmful content to reach protected AI models.
  • This can lead to data leaks and misinformation spread.
  • Attacks used character injection and adversarial ML evasion techniques.
  • The vulnerabilities risk undermining trust in AI safety systems.

item.title: OpenAI’s new browser Atlas falls for AI-targeted Cloaking Attack
item.description:
Author: Ivan Vlahov, Bastien Eymery
Date: Oct 25, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Web Security", "Artificial Intelligence", "Cybersecurity Threats", "Search Engine Optimization"]
Summary:
  • OpenAI’s Atlas browser is vulnerable to AI-targeted cloaking attacks.
  • Websites can show different content to AI crawlers and humans.
  • This manipulation poisons AI-generated summaries and reputations.
  • Attackers exploit user-agent detection to serve false narratives.
  • The threat impacts hiring, commerce, and recommendations.
  • Defenses include provenance signals and continuous AI output monitoring.
